subject: general
question: Which famous revolutionary set up base near Satar river in Jhansi in the 1920’s using the alias, Pandit Harishankar Brahmachari?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandrashekhar Azad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian revolutionary **Chandrashekhar Azad** set up a base near Satar river in Jhansi in the 1920s using the alias, Pandit Harishankar Brahmachari.
 
• Chandrashekhar Azad was born at **Bhabra village** in Madhya Pradesh on **23rd July 1906.**
 
• **Bhavra **also known as **Bhabhra or Chandra Shekhar Azad Nagar** is a town and a nagar panchayat in **Alirajpur** district in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**, where Azad reportedly lived incognito in the guise of a Sanyasi.
 
• Azad was involved in the 1925 **Kakori Conspiracy **wherein a train was robbed by **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).** 
 
• On **27 February 1931**, Azad was killed in a gun battle with two police officers at **Allahabad's Alfred Park.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Freedom Fighter**
 **Important Points**
 
 

 Bhagat Singh
 
 
In 1928, he established the** Hindustan Socialist Republican Association** (HSRA) along with Sukhdev, Chandrashekhar Azad, and others.

 
Bhagat Singh was also involved in the **Central Assembly Bombing Case**.

 
He was hanged on **23rd March 1931**. The day is observed as** ‘Martyrs’ Day**’ or ‘**Shaheed Diwas’** or ‘**Sarvodaya Day**.'

 
 
 

 Udham Singh
 
 
Udham Singh was a political activist who got associated with the** Ghadar Party** while in the US.

 
He killed** Michael O'Dwyer**, former lieutenant governor of the Punjab, India in London to avenge the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

 
He was hanged to death on** July 31, 1940,** for committing a murder.

 
 
 

 Khudiram Bose
 
 
Khudiram Bose was involved in the **Muzaffar bombing** to murder the Magistrate of Muzaffarpur, Kingsford.

 
On **11 August 1908**, one of India’s youngest revolutionary freedom fighters, Khudiram Bose was hanged by the British government (18 years of age).
